summary: Your supply work is a real stepping stone toward project management. You have already planned, tracked, and supervised, which are core parts of the job. The jump is moderate: what is missing is mostly formal project experience and a recognized certification.

transfers.from_experience: Unit Supply Specialist: ordering parts and following up until they arrived
transfers.why: Project managers keep work and materials arriving on time.

transfers.from_experience: Unit Supply Specialist: tracked and accounted for unit equipment
transfers.why: Project managers track budgets, equipment, and deliverables.

transfers.from_experience: Warehouse Supervisor: scheduled and supervised a team of warehouse associates
transfers.why: Project managers guide people who do not report to them and keep them on task.

transfers.from_experience: Unit Supply Specialist: trained junior team members on supply paperwork
transfers.why: Project managers bring new team members up to speed quickly.

gaps.item: This job usually expects a project management certification, such as CAPM or PMP.
gaps.how_to_close: Look into the CAPM, which is designed for people with no formal project experience, and check whether your military training already counts toward the required hours.

gaps.item: This job usually expects experience with project tools such as Microsoft Project, Jira, or Smartsheet.
gaps.how_to_close: Try a free trial of one tool and plan a small real project in it. If you have already used one, add it to your position.

gaps.item: This job usually expects budget and schedule responsibility.
gaps.how_to_close: If you ever managed spending, deadlines, or a project start to finish, add it to your position with the numbers.
